name: Attack on Pearl Harbor

sides.name: Empire of Japan
sides.commander: Isoroku Yamamoto (Combined Fleet), Chuichi Nagumo (1st Air Fleet), Mitsuo Fuchida (strike commander)
sides.strength: 6 fleet carriers, 2 battleships, 2 heavy cruisers, 1 light cruiser, 9 destroyers, 5 midget submarines, 353 aircraft in two waves
sides.casualties: 29 aircraft destroyed, 5 midget submarines lost, 64 killed

sides.name: United States
sides.commander: Husband E. Kimmel (Pacific Fleet), Walter Short (Hawaii Department)
sides.strength: 8 battleships, 8 cruisers, 30 destroyers in port; 390 aircraft on the airfields
sides.casualties: 2,403 killed (including 1,177 aboard USS Arizona), 1,178 wounded; 4 battleships sunk, 4 damaged; 188 aircraft destroyed

summary: Nagumo's task force launched the first strike of 183 aircraft from 230 nautical miles north of Oahu at 06:00. The attack arrived over Pearl Harbor at 07:55 and caught the fleet at anchor and the airfields with planes parked wingtip to wingtip. USS Arizona exploded when an armor-piercing bomb detonated her forward magazine. The second wave at 08:50 finished off USS Oklahoma and damaged the remaining battleships. By 09:55 the Japanese fleet was withdrawing. The American carriers, ferrying aircraft to outlying bases, had been at sea and were not present.
significance: Pearl Harbor brought the United States into the Second World War. Within days Germany and Italy declared war on the United States, completing the global alliance structure that would defeat the Axis four years later. Tactically the strike was a triumph; strategically it failed because it destroyed obsolete battleships while sparing the carriers and the fuel-tank farm, the assets that mattered most. Yamamoto reportedly remarked afterward that he feared they had "awakened a sleeping giant".
